perspective:
Bradley Ochoa’s available perspective:

- He knows he is a salesperson at a marketing firm. Katherine Lasiloo is his colleague and the marketing manager. He experiences their professional relationship as cordial but sometimes strained because they disagree about sales and marketing strategies.
- In the meeting room, he has prepared data and charts from the last five campaigns to support traditional sales techniques. He tells Katherine he appreciates her digital strategies but believes core sales would benefit more from traditional methods. He hears Katherine say the market is evolving, digital outreach has potential, and they should reconcile his data with increasing online engagement. He responds that he is not suggesting abandoning digital marketing, but feels proven methods are being sidelined without proper consideration. He hears Katherine suggest analyzing the data together and integrating both approaches.
- After the meeting, Katherine shares recent digital campaign success stories with improved engagement and sales. He hears her explain that it is about targeting the right audience with the right message and offering to walk him through analytics and decision-making. He becomes uncertain and open to learning, admits his doubts about moving away from traditional methods, and asks to understand the digital approach. He hears Katherine say she is glad he is open, that adaptation is important, and that they should dive deeper into the data.
- He later proposes a joint strategy meeting to integrate traditional and digital marketing. He hears Katherine agree, say combining strengths could lead to better results, and suggest scheduling a brainstorm. He tells her he is hopeful that leveraging both their expertise will be impactful and appreciates her willingness to collaborate. He hears Katherine say she looks forward to it and wants to leverage each other’s strengths.
- After the joint meeting, he is excited and works overtime to prepare a board presentation draft integrating both their ideas. He tells Katherine about the draft. He hears Katherine say it looks comprehensive, well thought out, and that his hard work shows. He says he is convinced the integrated approach will set them apart and wants to nail the presentation. He hears Katherine say she is confident and suggests fine-tuning it together.
- After the presentation and implementation, he feels grateful for his professional growth and the collaboration. He tells Katherine he has learned much from her and thanks her. He hears Katherine say it has been a pleasure, the project has come to fruition, and his openness made the partnership successful. He proposes regular strategy sessions. He hears Katherine agree, call it a fantastic idea, and say regular sessions will keep them on top of their game and market trends.

He does not have access to Katherine’s private thoughts, internal motivations, or narrator-only details about her personality, education, or background beyond what she says or does in their interactions.
